title: Hybrid sparse KV allocation and periodic defragmentation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview:
We observe sustained GPU memory fragmentation in high-concurrency workloads where continuous batching causes interleaved KV allocations of varied lengths. Small, non-contiguous KV slabs increase eviction churn and push down achievable batch sizes, increasing tail latency and per-token cost. This ticket defines a hybrid sparse-allocation + periodic defragmentation approach that minimizes in-flight stalls, bounds background work, and integrates with our continuous-batching pipeline and eviction policies.

Goals:
- Reduce fragmentation ratio (free holes vs total usable memory) by >= 50% for mixed-length workloads within first two minutes of steady state.
- Keep worst-case request latency impact from defrag below 5% of baseline.
- Avoid long GC-style pauses; background compaction must be incremental and preemptible.
- Retain compatibility with multi-tenant Dedicated pools and Private deployments where memory debugging may be limited.

Design summary:
1) Allocation strategy: "sparse-buckets"
- Maintain multiple fixed-size bucket classes (e.g., 64B, 256B, 1KB, 4KB, 16KB) tuned to observed KV lengths.
- For large KV blobs (> 16KB) use a direct-aligned allocation that is tracked separately.
- Buckets allocate from GPU page-aligned arenas to improve coalescing and reduce cross-page fragmentation.
- Each arena keeps a lightweight free-run-length bitset to allow O(1) allocation of contiguous runs for multi-chunk KVs used by attention cache.

2) Sparse placement policy:
- Prefer placing short-lived or high-turnover KV entries into dedicated "volatile" arenas which are compacted more aggressively.
- Long-lived or pinned entries go into "stable" arenas to avoid moving hot entries during compaction.
- Allocation tags capture lifetime hint (from runtime heuristics or LRU age) to drive placement.

3) Incremental background defragmentation ("micro-sweep"):
- A background executor scans arenas with fragmentation over a threshold (e.g., > 25%) and performs small, bounded copy/relocate operations (move N entries per tick).
- Moves are copy-on-write: we allocate target slots first, update a per-request indirection map, and then atomically flip the pointer so in-flight requests can continue using old location until they finish.
- The executor monitors request backlog and pauses if tail latency or queue size rises above safety thresholds.

4) Eviction and fallback integration:
- Evictions prefer reclaiming from volatile arenas first and coalesce freed adjacent runs into larger free ranges.
- When free memory falls below a critical watermark, we dynamically tighten the micro-sweep budget and trigger opportunistic full compaction on low-traffic windows (e.g., between batches).

5) Continuous batching-aware heuristics:
- Batcher exposes current batch window and expected next-token demand; defrag executor uses this to schedule heavier compaction during predicted low activity.
- For latency-sensitive requests with pinned KV usage, we prefer allocation that avoids moving pinned blocks (stable arenas).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Why hybrid buckets? Pure slab or pure buddy allocators either produce internal waste (slab) or slow allocations and fragmentation under varied sizes (buddy). Hybrid buckets with arena-level run bitsets balance speed and packing efficiency for KV shapes common in attention caches.
- Copy-on-write movement increases short-term memory usage by a small factor (target 5-10%) but avoids stop-the-world pauses and preserves correctness for multi-threaded request paths.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for bucket allocation & run-length bitset correctness (simulated multi-threaded allocation patterns).
- Synthetic workloads: mix of small ephemeral KVs (chatty completion workloads) and large persistent KVs (long conversations), measure fragmentation, eviction rate, throughput.
- Integration test with continuous batching harness to ensure micro-sweep pauses when backlog increases.
- GPU memory stress test on Dedicated pool images and on a Private single-node to validate alignment assumptions.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal dogfood): feature gated off, run on 5% of runtime-1.20 nightly clusters for 72h with shadow traffic and collection of fragmentation/latency metrics.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for small production subset for non-critical customers with detailed telemetry dashboards.
- Phase 2: gradual ramp with opt-out toggle; monitor tail latency and memory metrics for regressions.

Observability and metrics:
- Fragmentation ratio per arena (free_contiguous_bytes / arena_size).
- Move rate (entries relocated per minute) and bytes moved per minute.
- Background executor CPU/GPU time and pause counts due to safety throttle.
- Eviction count per arena and eviction latency.
- End-user P50/P95/P99 latency and per-token cost delta.

Implementation notes / artifacts:
- Prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feat/hybrid-sparse-kv (PR: #4728 - WIP).
- Design doc: docs/internal/kv-hybrid-sparse-defrag-2026.md (Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kv-hybrid-defrag).
- Benchmark dashboard: internal Grafana panel "kv_alloc_defrag_v1".

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Exact bucket cutpoints and arena sizes need calibration from 2 weeks of telemetry; we should run offline clustering on recent KV length histograms.
- Safety margins for copy-on-write overhead in very memory-tight Dedicated pools (customers with small GPU reservations) — will require additional opt-in flags.
- Interaction with cross-GPU KV sharding and NVLink peer-to-peer moves (we currently assume intra-GPU moves are fast; cross-device relocation needs different path).

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated tests cover allocation, relocation correctness, and safety pause behavior.
- Dogfood runs show >= 40% reduction in fragmentation ratio and no >2% increase in P99 latency.
- Rollout plan ready with toggles, dashboards, and runbook entries for outage/rollback.
